title: CRLR/128/2017 of Anand Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
CRMA No. 3785/2019 (Second Bail Application)
In
CRLR No. 128 of 2017
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Sachin, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, Brief Holder for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate for
respondent no. 2.
The present criminal revision has been
preferred by the convict-revisionist, who has
been convicted in complaint case registered
by respondent no. 2 by way of Criminal
Complaint Case No. 685 of 2015 'Dan Singh
vs. Anand Singh'. As a consequence thereto,
he had been convicted to undergo a sentence
of six months of rigorous imprisonment and
a fine of Rs. 3,40,000/- has been imposed
upon him. In an event of default of payment
of fine, he had been directed to further
undergo one month of simple imprisonment.
The said judgment of conviction dated
26.10.2016 was affirmed in Criminal Appeal
No. 210 of 2016 'Anand Singh vs Dan Singh
and Another' by the judgment dated
01.05.2017 resulting into dismissal of the
criminal appeal.
During the pendency of the revision,
whatever financial liability was levied upon
the revisionist by way of a penalty by the
judgments impugned under challenge, it is
the fact, which is admitted by the learned
counsel for the respondent no. 2 that the
entire financial liability has been paid back
to him by the revisionist.
Now the question is as to whether in
this situation, where the financial liability
has already been discharged, still the
revisionist should be directed to undergo a
sentence and that too in complaint case
where the complainant admits the remittance

of the liability and does not want to
prosecute the revisionist for the offence
under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments
Act.
Hence, on account of the subsequent
development and in view of the statement
made by the learned counsel for the
respondent/complainant, that the entire
amount has been remitted to the
complainant, this revision is allowed. The
impugned order of conviction is quashed.
The penalty as it has been directed by the
courts below has been remitted by the
revisionist.
Apart from the amount, which was
directed to be remitted to the State
Exchequer, that would still be discharged by
the revisionist by remitting an amount of Rs.
10,000/- as directed therewith in the State
treasury. The effect of acquittal as a
consequence of its judgment would only be
subject to depositing the penalty amount in
the treasury to the tune of Rs. 10,000/-.
Subject to above observations,
revision is allowed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 03.12.2019
Pooja
